name: IDFV and App Set ID (developer-scoped IDs)
plain: A per-developer app ID that needs no prompt but cannot cross to other companies' apps.
meaning: Lets one developer recognize the same device across its own apps for analytics, fraud and fair-use limits. Not allowed for ad targeting on Android and not usable for third-party tracking on iOS.

android.persistence: Resets after 13 months of no use or when the developer's apps are all removed
android.store_policy: Play Ads policy: App Set ID for analytics and fraud, not ad personalization or attribution
android.note: Replaces persistent IDs for non-ad uses when the ad ID is zeroed.

ios.persistence: Same value for apps sharing a team prefix; resets when the last app of that vendor is removed
ios.store_policy: Counts as an identifier in privacy labels if linked to the person

limits.headline: Can recognise your phone across one company's apps, but not other companies' apps
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when the app starts
can: Tell that two apps from the same developer are on the same phone
Count users, spot fraud and set fair use limits
Stand in for the ad ID on Android for non ad uses when the ad ID is zeroed
cannot: Follow you into apps from other companies
Be used for ad targeting on Android or for third party tracking on iPhone
Show a prompt; none is needed
limits.differs: iPhone calls it IDFV. Android calls it App Set ID.

story.what_it_is: A number that lets one developer recognize your phone across its own apps, with no prompt.

marketing.name: Identifier for Vendor
marketing.pitch: A unique ID the same for all of a developer's apps on a device.

marketing.name: App Set ID
marketing.pitch: A reset, developer scoped ID for analytics and fraud, not for ads.

story.for_you: You never see it. It lets a company that makes several apps know it is the same phone, so a fraud limit or a free trial can apply across all of them.
story.for_makers: It needs no prompt and cannot join other companies' apps, so it is a safe way to run analytics, stop abuse and enforce fair use. Apple and Google both bar it from ad targeting.

use_cases.example: A studio that makes five games gives a welcome bonus only once per phone across all five.
A fraud team sees a phone create 40 accounts in a day and blocks it.
A company with a main app and a lite app counts one user instead of two.
An office suite keeps your settings in sync across its sister apps.
A retailer avoids showing the same coupon twice to one phone.
A developer groups crash reports by device across its apps.

risks: Stable across reinstall until all apps removed
story.android_note: Android calls its version the App Set ID, which resets after 13 months idle.
story.ios_note: iOS calls it the IDFV, and it resets when the last app from that developer is deleted.

technical_bounds: Cannot join with other developers' apps
Not a substitute for the ad ID in ads on Android
iOS: ATT does not apply while the ID is not combined with third-party data

abuse: Used with MMP identity graphs to simulate cross-app IDs

history.change: App Set ID introduced via Play services as the recommended non-ad ID
